title: Talent Acquisition Essentials
subject: Human Resources
description: Define roles clearly, source candidates through the right channels, run structured interviews, and give every candidate a good experience.

lessons.title: Defining the role before you hire
lessons.body:
Good hiring starts with a clear role. Before advertising, agree with the hiring manager on:

- **Purpose:** why the role exists and what it must achieve in its first year.
- **Key responsibilities:** five to seven outcomes, not a long list of tasks.
- **Must-have skills and experience:** what the candidate needs on day one.
- **Nice-to-have skills:** what can be learned after joining.

A vague job description attracts the wrong applicants and wastes interview time. Write it once with the manager, and keep it as the reference for every interview.

lessons.title: Sourcing candidates
lessons.body:
Use several sourcing channels, since each brings different candidates:

- **Employee referrals:** often the best quality and retention, so reward them fairly.
- **Job portals and professional networks:** wide reach, but more noise to filter.
- **Direct sourcing:** searching for people with the right skills, then making contact.
- **Campus and community programmes:** a pipeline for entry-level and technical roles.

Track the source of every hire. Over time, that data shows which channels bring the best results for each role type.

lessons.title: Structured interviews
lessons.body:
Structured interviews ask every candidate the same core questions, scored against the same criteria. Research on hiring consistently finds that structured interviews predict job performance better than unstructured conversations.

Steps:

1. Choose four to six competencies from the role definition.
2. Write two or three questions for each, asking for specific past examples.
3. Score each answer against a shared scale, such as 1 to 4, with notes.
4. Discuss scores with the panel before making a decision.

Avoid questions about age, marital status, religion, or other protected characteristics, and avoid questions unrelated to the job.

lessons.title: Candidate experience
lessons.body:
Every candidate is also a potential customer and a possible future employee. A poor experience spreads quickly.

Simple practices that improve experience:

- Acknowledge every application.
- Give a realistic timeline and keep to it.
- Tell candidates clearly what happens at each stage.
- Give feedback to finalists, even when the answer is no.
- Confirm offers in writing promptly.

Candidates who feel well treated refer others and remain positive about the company even when they are not hired.

questions.text: What should a role definition focus on?
options: A long list of every task
Purpose, key outcomes, and must-have skills
correct: Purpose, key outcomes, and must-have skills

questions.text: Which sourcing channel often gives the best quality and retention?

options: It is held in a formal room
Every candidate is asked the same core questions and scored on the same criteria
The interviewer chooses questions on the day
correct: Every candidate is asked the same core questions and scored on the same criteria

questions.text: Which practices improve candidate experience? (Select all that apply)
Interview questions about a candidate's religion are acceptable if they are asked to every candidate.
